life_summary: Delbert Todd Christofferson was born on January 24, 1945, in American Fork, Utah. He grew up in the Intermountain West and pursued legal studies, eventually earning a law degree. Christofferson's professional career included a notable position as law clerk to U.S. Federal Judge John Sirica during the Watergate scandal (1972–1974), where he witnessed firsthand the constitutional and legal complexities surrounding one of America's greatest political crises. He worked as an attorney in Salt Lake City before dedicating himself to full-time Church service. In 1968, he married Katherine Jacob at the Salt Lake Temple, and the couple raised five children together while building a life centered on both professional accomplishment and deep religious commitment.
church_summary: Christofferson served in a two-year mission to Argentina under mission president Richard G. Scott before pursuing legal studies. He was called as a member of the Presidency of the Seventy and later as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 2009. His ministry has included significant work on family history and sensitive negotiations with Jewish leaders regarding Church policies on temple work for Holocaust victims, demonstrating his commitment to both theological integrity and interfaith respect. His legal background has informed his approach to policy matters within the Church administration, and his teachings have emphasized the importance of family relationships and eternal covenants.
